body_text:
Direct images and preimages interact with Boolean operations
according to fundamental preservation laws:
- *Preimages preserve all Boolean structure*: for any family of
subsets $B_i \subseteq B$,
$$f^{-1}\left[\bigcup_{i \in I} B_i\right] = \bigcup_{i \in I} f^{-1}[B_i], \quad f^{-1}\left[\bigcap_{i \in I} B_i\right] = \bigcap_{i \in I} f^{-1}[B_i]$$
and $f^{-1}[B \setminus Y] = A \setminus f^{-1}[Y]$.
- *Direct images preserve unions*: $f\left[\bigcup_{i \in I} A_i\right] = \bigcup_{i \in I} f[A_i]$.
- *Direct images preserve intersections only as inclusions in general*:
$f\left[\bigcap_{i \in I} A_i\right] \subseteq \bigcap_{i \in I} f[A_i]$.
Equality holds for all families if and only if $f$ is injective.
